name: Giant Peg
description: A four-metre wooden clothes peg set in a plinth on a terracotta plaza.
lighting: Hard midday sun, one crisp short shadow
subject: either
prompt: One monumental wooden clothes peg, about four metres tall, stands upright on the tips of its jaws, set into a low square plinth of terracotta tile that holds it as steady as any public sculpture on a flat terracotta-tiled plaza. It is built exactly as a real clothes peg is, only larger: two matching pale wooden halves pressed shut at the jaws by one coiled steel spring seated in the notches at their waist, well above head height, its wire arms lying flat along the outer faces and flashing in the sun. The sky behind is a hard, cloudless cobalt. Hard midday sun gives the peg one crisp short shadow on the tiles, and the tile joints run in true perspective toward the horizon. The palette is pale wood, terracotta and cobalt, witty, warm and bold.
